- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via HookSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d3bea96d8531495c9d1c0f1c69d58308dda74433` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `05d7592d92cf51e19eeb4ad78b365a911d4f61a0` — the merge of head `1621f1e9988c42e089fd2de9115b41a0a96a4426` into base `d3bea96d8531495c9d1c0f1c69d58308dda74433`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 05d7592d92cf51e19eeb4ad78b365a911d4f61a0 && git checkout 05d7592d92cf51e19eeb4ad78b365a911d4f61a0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d3bea96d8531495c9d1c0f1c69d58308dda74433 1621f1e9988c42e089fd2de9115b41a0a96a4426 && git checkout -B drift-repro d3bea96d8531495c9d1c0f1c69d58308dda74433 && git merge --no-ff 1621f1e9988c42e089fd2de9115b41a0a96a4426

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d3bea96d8531495c9d1c0f1c69d58308dda74433
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d3bea96d8531495c9d1c0f1c69d58308dda74433` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `709b3aeea17aa4b50a6cf985be96a6d65684287e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/hook-wrappers.ts, packages/objectql/src/unit-detach.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-transactions-section.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-scoped-context.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts

PR #34043 (card #33760), net diff against `main` at merge base `b4ce310b88`. Read: the card body and its five comments (claim 6895293301, pre-claim 6895342679, reports 6897959918 and 6898170253, declaration correction 6897999027), the PR body, the ten-file diff, and the 67 check-runs on this head (every one `success` or `skipped`, none failed or pending). Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `hook-run-as.ts`, `engine-hook-dispatch.ts`, `engine-middleware-and-context.ts`, `engine-driver-options.ts`, `skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md`, `AGENTS.md` Post-Task step 3, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Published accept set: unchanged. Right.** `hook.zod.ts` changes TSDoc only: no `.describe()` string, no schema shape, no default. `Spec property liveness` and `Check Changeset` are green and no generated baseline is in the diff.
- **Public surface of `@objectstack/objectql`: unchanged. Right.** `unit-detach.ts` is not re-exported from the package entry (`git grep unit-detach` on `src/index.ts` is empty). The new `UNIT_ROLLED_BACK`, `UnitCommitQueue` and the queue helpers are module-internal. `ScopedContext#[DETACHED_HOOK_RUN]` changed its signature, and its key is an unexported unique symbol. `runOpenedUnit` and `openedUnits` are `private`.
- **Authorable meaning of `async: true`: changed. Right, and declared.** Inside an engine-owned unit the handler used to start at dispatch and now starts after the outermost commit, or never. That is a changed meaning of an existing key with no new key or value, so `semantic` is the right kind (AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3) and `none` would under-declare it.
- **The four units the `HookEvent` docblock names all reach the queue. Right.** The door's unit (`engine-hook-dispatch.ts:80`), the atomic cascade (`engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts:654`, `:750`), atomic batches and a caller's `engine.transaction()` all go through `ObjectQL.transaction()`. `ctx.api.transaction()` goes through `ScopedContext.transaction()` or the trio. Each opens and settles a queue.
- **One derived judgment is wrong:** the claim that every async after-hook fired in such a unit waits for the commit. See ④ finding 1.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no` is right. Nothing in the diff is a published accept set or an export, and nothing a caller of the triggering write receives moves, because nothing waits for an async hook. The `(narrowing)` arm is rightly declined: no value an author writes is refused and no caller answer goes from served to refused.
- `Metadata-protocol: semantic` is right, as above. Both lines are in the PR body and in the changeset body.
- Level is right. `@objectstack/objectql: minor` satisfies "a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves", and `@objectstack/spec: patch` is correct for shipped TSDoc. The gate's own rule is at least one moved package graded `minor` or above, and `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on this head.
- `Skills-docs:` is owed (the kind is not `none`) and is present. Its reason is true for what it cites and incomplete: see ④ finding 2.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The two `open_questions` of report 6897959918 (which Clause-② line, which Metadata-protocol line) were answered by the area in 6897999027. Both answers are judged right in ②. Report 6898170253 carries none.
- Deviation "the trio got a queue too": inside the claimed surface (`packages/objectql/src/**`) and necessary, since the sandbox runner's `ctx.api.transaction(fn)` uses the trio. Accepted.
- Deviation "ride-along comment fix in `hook-after-abort-rollback.dogfood.test.ts`": added to the file surface by 6897999027. Lane seat's ACCEPT.
- Deviation "derived gate sweep not repeated after the merge": moot. The check-runs on this head are the gate verdicts and all are green.
- Out-of-scope note "`HookContext.transaction` in a deferred run still exposes the committed handle": unchanged by this diff, and harmless since `isDetachedUnitHandle` treats it as absent. No escalation.
- `skills/**` is untouched, so the PR is not on the governed register through that path.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`**, sentence by sentence against the code:

- "A blocking hook's `ctx.api` / `ctx.ql` writes join the same transaction and roll back with everything else": holds (unchanged behaviour).
- "An `async: true` hook is the exception: it runs after the unit commits and not at all if it rolls back, so its writes are never part of the unit": holds for every hook whose `ctx.api` is an engine `ScopedContext`. **Does not hold in the case of finding 1.**
- "an async hook starts once the outermost unit commits": holds. A nested `transaction()` joins (both surfaces and the trio check the ambient entry first) and opens no queue. `settleUnitCommitQueue(queue, true)` runs after `commit` returns and outside the `try`, so a waiting run cannot reach the rollback path. **Except finding 1.**
- "and is dropped without running when that unit rolls back": holds. Both `catch` arms settle with `false` before the driver rollback, including when the commit itself throws. **Except finding 1.**
- "its `ctx.api` reads then see the committed write, and its writes run outside the unit, on their own connection": holds. The start is bound to the dispatch context with `AsyncResource.bind` and then leaves the ambient store through `runOutsideOpenUnits`.
- "Outside any unit it starts at once, after the write": holds. With no unsettled queue, `runOutsideOpenUnitsOnCommit` calls `runOutsideOpenUnits` synchronously, and the wrapper hands over the context by reference as before.
- "Nothing waits for it, and its errors never reach the caller": holds. The settle never awaits, and each start is wrapped in `try`/`catch` and a `.catch`.

Break attempts that did not break it: nested inner return with outer rollback; a dispatch between the callback settling and the commit (the entry keeps its queue after `runOpenedUnit` closes the handle); a hook started after commit that fires another async hook (the queue's `pending` is `undefined`, and its handle is detached, so it starts at once); a unit the deferred hook opens itself (new handle, own queue); a primitive handle (the ambient entry still carries the queue); a write routed to another datasource inside the unit (refused by `enforceTransactionOrigin`, so no landed write loses its hook).

**Finding 1, must-fix. An `async: true` hook with `runAs: 'user'` whose trigger carries no user still starts at dispatch, inside the unit, and still runs when the unit rolls back.**

- `hook-wrappers.ts:531` passes `detached.api` to `runDetachedHook`. For `runAs: 'user'`, `installRunAsApi` has already replaced `ctx.api` with the derived api, and `ScopedContextFacet.withRunAs` (`engine-scoped-context.ts:130`) returns `new UnscopedHookApi(ref)` when `executionContext.userId` is absent.
- `UnscopedHookApi` (`hook-run-as.ts:141`) has no `[DETACHED_HOOK_RUN]` member, so `runDetachedHook` (`unit-detach.ts:216`) takes its "cannot detach" arm and returns `body()` at once. No queue is consulted, not even the ambient one.
- Reachable with schema-valid metadata: an after-hook declaring `async: true, runAs: 'user'`, fired by a write made with a system context (a seed, a job, a flow run) inside `engine.transaction()`, an atomic batch, or the door's unit beside a blocking hook.
- Effect: the handler runs before the commit and after a rollback. Its `ctx.api` data doors refuse, so it cannot write through the engine, but a handler that makes an external effect first (a webhook, a queue message) announces a write that was undone. That is the exact outcome the `async` TSDoc ("dropped without running"), the `HookEvent` bullet ("not at all if it rolls back") and the changeset ("an external effect it makes ... is never announced for a write that was undone") say cannot happen.
- No pin covers it: the only `runAs` in the new tests is `'system'`.
- Fix direction: decide the unit from the engine-built api (the `original` the wrapper held before the install), or give `UnscopedHookApi` the detach key bound to the context it was derived from; add a pin for commit and for rollback. Stating the exception in the TSDoc and changeset instead would also make the contract true, and is the weaker fix.

**Finding 2, should-fix (PR body only, the head does not move). `Skills-docs: none` covers half of the change.** `data-hooks.md:64` does say "in the background, after commit", so the cited reason is true. The skill says nothing about the other half: an async hook is dropped when the unit rolls back, so it can no longer be used to react to a refused write. The changeset tells human upgraders this, and an AI author reading the skill is not told. The line should read `follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md` so the seat files the skills card.

**Finding 3, nit. The unchanged opening of the `HookEvent` docblock now contradicts the edited bullet for async hooks.** The heading "`after*` fires INSIDE the unit of work, not after it commits", "a later refusal can roll the row back after the hook has already run", and the "Effects OUTSIDE the engine" bullet ("the announcement has already gone out") are unqualified, and they are no longer true of an `async: true` hook. The edited bullet names the exception, so a careful reader recovers. One clause in the opening paragraph would remove the contradiction. Fold it into the finding 1 round.

**Finding 4, nit. A late write in the window between the callback settling and a commit that then fails loses its async hook.** In that window the unit's handle is closed, so a write from work the callback did not await lands outside the unit, while its async after-hook is queued on the unit and dropped when the commit fails. The window is the duration of the commit and needs both un-awaited work and a commit failure. Accepted deviation, or a follow-up card.

**Finding 5, nit. A deferred run's execution metric includes the wait for the commit.** `recordOutcome` measures from `startedAt`, taken at dispatch. Accepted deviation.

**Implementing files, otherwise:** `unit-detach.ts`, `engine-transactions-section.ts`, `engine-scoped-context.ts` and `engine.ts` agree with the contract. The trio settles on its own commit and rollback, and a handle whose commit throws with no rollback after it keeps its runs unstarted, which the PR body states. `hook-wrappers.ts` agrees except for finding 1: the copy taken at dispatch correctly keeps the flat input and the derived api for a deferred run.

- If a commit fails, a late write that was not awaited loses its async hook.
- A deferred run's metric includes the wait for the commit.

Two pins (commit, rollback) assert the handler got `UnscopedHookApi` and still waited or was dropped.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Published accept set: unchanged. Right.** `hook.zod.ts` moves TSDoc only: no `.describe()` string, no shape, no default. `TypeScript Type Check` (which holds the spec's generated-artifact gates), `Spec property liveness` and `Check Changeset` are `success` on this head, and no generated baseline needs to be in the diff for a TSDoc-only change.

- **Every unit-of-work door reaches one queue. Right.** The door's own unit (`engine-hook-dispatch.ts:80`), both atomic cascade wraps (`engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts:654`, `:750`), the REST atomic batch (`rest/src/batch-routes.ts:512`), the metadata repository, recycle-bin restore, plugin-auth, storage and messaging all open their unit through `ObjectQL.transaction()` or `ScopedContext.transaction()`; the sandbox runner goes through the trio. A nested call on any of the three joins the ambient unit and opens no queue. ### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`, against the code.** For a write event every sentence of the new prose holds: start after the outermost commit (the settle runs after `commit` returns, outside the `try`); dropped on rollback (both `catch` arms settle with `false` before the driver rollback, a failed commit included); nested returns are no commit; outside a unit the run starts at once and by reference as before; nothing awaits a run; a run's failure is recorded and logged by the wrapper's `.catch`, never swallowed silently and never thrown into `transaction()`. Order is dispatch order, each run started before `transaction()` returns. A deferred run gets a copy of the hook context taken at dispatch, bound to the dispatch's async context, so it sees the same user, tenant and identity stores and the api its `runAs` is owed. Break attempts that held: nested inner return with outer rollback; a hook started after commit dispatching another async hook; a unit opened by a deferred hook; a primitive handle; `runAs` user-less (the prior must-fix); an app-authored derived api.

**M1 (must-fix) — the deferral and the drop also apply to `afterFind`, and nothing declares or pins that.** New; no prior id.

- The rule the code must keep: a hook on a read event must not lose its run to the outcome of a unit the read does not belong to, unless the contract says so in words an author will read. A read is not undone by a rollback; the rows were already returned.
- The tree does not keep it. `async` is honoured for every event whose name starts with `after` (`hook-wrappers.ts:311`, `:387`), `afterFind` is built with the engine api like the write events (`engine-find.ts:536`, `:831`), and the queue does not look at the event. An `async: true` `afterFind` hook fired by a read inside any engine unit now waits for that unit's commit and does not run when it rolls back. Before this head it ran.
- Nothing says so. The `async` TSDoc speaks of "the committed write" and "after the write"; the `HookEvent` section it points to is scoped to `afterInsert` / `afterUpdate` / `afterDelete`; the changeset names only writes; the reason given for the drop ("it never announces a write that was rolled back") does not apply to a read. No pin fires `afterFind` in a unit, for commit or for rollback.
- Fix direction: either keep read events out of the drop (start at dispatch as before, or start when the unit settles whatever its outcome), or state it in the `async` TSDoc and the changeset, with what an author who records reads must do instead. Either way pin `afterFind` inside a unit for both outcomes, with the outside-unit CONTROL.
